notes: §1985:VIII.4.3.2 prints "DELETE file-name-1 RECORD [INVALID KEY ...] [NOT INVALID KEY ...] [END-DELETE]" in that sequence (§1985:IV.2.1). CobolIO.g4#deleteStatement parses the superset and KeyedIoBinder#BindDelete binds the INVALID/NOT INVALID pair; at 85 VersionConformancePass#VisitConditionalPhrases (ConditionalPhrases#OutOfPrintedOrder) refuses NOT INVALID KEY before INVALID KEY (COBOL0900), VisitRetryPhrase refuses RETRY and VisitDeleteFileStatement refuses DELETE FILE, and a repeated INVALID KEY is COBOL2269. Probes at --std 85: b) reversed order COBOL0900, INVALID KEY twice COBOL2269, NOT INVALID KEY alone COBOL6826 (SR2); c) RETRY 3 TIMES and DELETE FILE both COBOL0900; e) RANDOM and DYNAMIC run INVALID KEY on key 0 and on a deleted record (status 23) and NOT INVALID KEY on success, SEQUENTIAL with INVALID KEY COBOL1720 (SR1), SEQUENTIAL without it deletes the last-read record (00, then AT END 10), DELETE of a closed file gives 49 with no INVALID KEY branch; a) a RECORD VARYING DEPENDING ON file with an ODO record keeps the record area and the DEPENDING ON item unchanged (GR5); d) and f) do not apply to a format with no data operand. The witness deletes key 2 twice in RANDOM mode and prints DELETED then NOT FOUND. The prior PARTIAL (NOT INVALID KEY accepted before INVALID KEY) is fixed by kb/Work PB5158 (landed), reprobed here. History: until the 1985 re-read 5 (2026-11-14) this row read PARTIAL, naming no kb/Work note; the re-read of main dc1f2dcce8 found that defect fixed by the landing of kb/Work PB5158 and records CONFORMS, upheld by an independent refuter (code read: op-20261114/out-reread5/rs-11.json, refuter op-20261114/out-reread5/rs-11-refute.json).

next.reason: 1985: "DELETE file-name-1 RECORD [ INVALID KEY imperative-statement-1 ] [ NOT INVALID KEY imperative-statement-2 ]"; 2023: "DELETE file-name-1 RECORD [ retry-phrase ] ┌ │ INVALID KEY imperative-statement-1 │ ┐ … NOT INVALID KEY imperative-statement-2". 2023 Format 1 adds an optional retry-phrase. Its choice indicators also let INVALID KEY and NOT INVALID KEY appear in either order, where 1985 fixed the order, so more programs are accepted.
